# Maintenance Report — MNT-0140-021

**Asset:** WELL-0140 (NE-07 Well 140, T200, Northeast Block 7)
**Equipment:** wellhead
**Work started:** 09 Jan 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 14 Jan 2026 06:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 118 hours
**Crew lead:** Megan Ward (U-305) · **Crew:** Brian Coleman · **Contractor:** Coyote Ridge Well Services
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0140-0166 on 2026-01-08
**Report written:** 15 Jan 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0140-0166 showed the wellhead at 16.9 °C with the air at 11.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored.
The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

Normal packing wear.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
2. Removed the old packing.
3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

## Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0103-025

**Asset:** WELL-0103 (NE-07 Well 103, T350, Northeast Block 7)
**Equipment:** flowline
**Work started:** 17 Jan 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 10 Feb 2026 16:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 584 hours
**Crew lead:** Megan Ward (U-305) · **Crew:** Daniel Foster · **Contractor:** Tumbleweed Flowline Co.
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0103-0169 on 2026-01-15
**Report written:** 10 Feb 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0103-0169 showed the wellhead at 16.8 °C with the air at 9.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 328 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 262 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0103-025 (WS-06).

**Report written:** 09 Oct 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0261-0200 showed the wellhead at 36.3 °C with the air at 32.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.

5. Greased all structural bearings.

## Testing and return to service

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0109-0209 showed the wellhead at 24.2 °C with the air at 16.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

## Testing and return to service

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0114-025

**Asset:** WELL-0114 (NE-07 Well 114, T350, Northeast Block 7)
**Equipment:** flowline
**Work started:** 02 Oct 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 06 Oct 2026 19:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 107 hours
**Crew lead:** Megan Ward (U-305) · **Crew:** Brian Coleman, Kevin Price · **Contractor:** Tumbleweed Flowline Co.
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0114-0204 on 2026-10-01
**Report written:** 07 Oct 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0114-0204 showed the wellhead at 30.0 °C with the air at 23.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 336 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 269 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0114-025 (WS-06).

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0133-0182 showed the wellhead at 23.6 °C with the air at 20.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. # Maintenance Report — MNT-0116-012

**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 24 Apr 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 18 May 2026 20:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 588 hours
**Crew lead:** Daniel Foster (U-302) · **Crew:** Kevin Price, Brian Coleman
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0116-0103 on 2026-04-23
**Report written:** 20 May 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0116-0103 showed the wellhead at 29.7 °C with the air at 24.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

## Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

## Work done

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

## Testing and return to service

Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0159-0177 on 2026-03-19
**Report written:** 27 Mar 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0159-0177 showed the wellhead at 21.3 °C with the air at 14.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit.
The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.
This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

## Work done

1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0160-0194 on 2026-07-30
**Report written:** 27 Aug 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0160-0194 showed the wellhead at 36.1 °C with the air at 35.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit.
The well stayed shut in for about 24 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

## Safety and permits

## Work done

1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

## What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0193-0199 showed the wellhead at 42.9 °C with the air at 35.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 350 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 280 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0166-0207 showed the wellhead at 23.6 °C with the air at 17.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. ## What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0262-0170 showed the wellhead at 12.3 °C with the air at 11.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

**Asset:** WELL-0258 (NE-08 Well 258, T200, Northeast Block 8)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 14 Feb 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 09 Mar 2026 21:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 565 hours
**Crew lead:** Brian Coleman (U-304) · **Crew:** Kevin Price, Megan Ward
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0258-0171 on 2026-02-12
**Report written:** 10 Mar 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0258-0171 showed the wellhead at 8.6 °C with the air at 6.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.
The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0258-027 (WS-06).

## Parts and cost

| Item | USD |
|---|---|
| Gearbox seal kit | 891 |
| Gear oil | 792 |
| Absorbent pads | 296 |
| Labour (company crew) | 1,202 |
| **Total** | **3,181** |

## Compliance check

| Protocol | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| WS-01 | Met | Meeting held and recorded |
| WS-02 | Met | Energy isolated and tagged |
| WS-03 | Met | Monitors bump-tested; highest 1 ppm |
| WS-06 | Met | Oily waste manifested to an approved site |
| WS-07 | Met | Written 1 day after the work (limit 3 days) |

## Notes and recommendations

- Check the gearbox oil level monthly on this unit.
- Used oil and pads shipped as oily waste.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0298-027

**Asset:** WELL-0298 (NE-08 Well 298, T350, Northeast Block 8)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 22 Mar 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 07 Apr 2026 08:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 384 hours
**Crew lead:** Megan Ward (U-305) · **Crew:** Kevin Price · **Contractor:** Coyote Ridge Well Services
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0298-0174 on 2026-03-19
**Report written:** 08 Apr 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0298-0174 showed the wellhead at 21.3 °C with the air at 18.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 14 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.
This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

## Parts and cost

| Item | USD |
|---|---|
| Saddle bearing assembly | 1,330 |
| Bolts, shims and seals | 333 |
| Bearing grease and consumables | 554 |
| Labour (company crew and contractor) | 2,555 |
| **Total** | **4,772** |

## Compliance check

| Protocol | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| WS-01 | Met | Meeting held and recorded |
| WS-02 | Met | Energy isolated and tagged |
| WS-03 | Met | Monitors bump-tested; highest 2 ppm |
| WS-07 | Met | Written 1 day after the work (limit 3 days) |
| Manual §10 | Action required | 3 corrective repairs on this equipment in 12 months; root-cause analysis to be started |

## Notes and recommendations

- Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
- Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
- Start a root-cause analysis for this equipment before the next repair is closed (well-type manual, section 10).

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0156-024

**Asset:** WELL-0156 (NE-08 Well 156, T200, Northeast Block 8)
**Equipment:** flowline
**Work started:** 18 Apr 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 22 Apr 2026 04:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 92 hours
**Crew lead:** Daniel Foster (U-302) · **Crew:** Brian Coleman
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0156-0180 on 2026-04-16
**Report written:** 22 Apr 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0156-0180 showed the wellhead at 21.9 °C with the air at 21.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 280 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 224 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0156-024 (WS-06).

| **Total** | **4,840** |

## Compliance check

| WS-02 | Met | Energy isolated and tagged |
| WS-03 | Met | Monitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm |
| WS-04 | Met | Permit issued; gas test 0% LEL |
| WS-05 | Met | Tested at 1.25 × maximum operating pressure, held 4 hours |
| WS-06 | Met | Oily waste manifested to an approved site |
| WS-07 | Met | Written the same day as the work (limit 3 days) |

- Check wall thickness along the rest of this flowline.
- Consider corrosion inhibitor injection.

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0175-0173 on 2026-03-05
**Report written:** 20 Mar 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0175-0173 showed the wellhead at 17.8 °C with the air at 15.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 10 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

## Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 189 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 151 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0175-028 (WS-06).

## What happened

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0178-0167 showed the wellhead at 10.0 °C with the air at 10.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

## Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

## Work done

2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0411-023

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0411-0141 on 2026-12-03
**Report written:** 12 Jan 2027

## What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0411-0141 showed the wellhead at 22.7 °C with the air at 10.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 34 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.
This is corrective repair number 5 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: ESP drive stopped, drive disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0325-0174 on 2026-02-26

## What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0325-0174 showed the wellhead at 16.7 °C with the air at 12.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.
This is corrective repair number 5 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

## Work done

2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0449-029

**Asset:** WELL-0449 (NW-12 Well 449, T200, Northwest Block 12)
**Equipment:** flowline
**Work started:** 24 Apr 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 28 Apr 2026 02:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 90 hours
**Crew lead:** Daniel Foster (U-302) · **Crew:** Brian Coleman, Megan Ward
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0449-0179 on 2026-04-23
**Report written:** 30 Apr 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0449-0179 showed the wellhead at 27.1 °C with the air at 22.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 271 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 217 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0449-029 (WS-06).

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0348-032

**Asset:** WELL-0348 (NW-12 Well 348, T200, Northwest Block 12)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 15 May 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 09 Jun 2026 03:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 595 hours
**Crew lead:** Megan Ward (U-305) · **Crew:** Kevin Price · **Contractor:** Coyote Ridge Well Services
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0348-0184 on 2026-05-14
**Report written:** 10 Jun 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0348-0184 showed the wellhead at 34.9 °C with the air at 29.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

**Follow-up:** Crew to return within 7 days to check the bearing temperature and re-grease the unit.

## Work done

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

| Bolts, shims and seals | 396 |
| Bearing grease and consumables | 661 |
| Labour (company crew and contractor) | 2,322 |
| **Total** | **4,965** |

## Compliance check

## Notes and recommendations

- Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
- Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0310-0186 showed the wellhead at 32.7 °C with the air at 31.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0377-029

**Asset:** WELL-0377 (NW-12 Well 377, T350, Northwest Block 12)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 25 Apr 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 29 Apr 2026 06:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 94 hours
**Crew lead:** Kevin Price (U-303) · **Crew:** Brian Coleman · **Contractor:** Coyote Ridge Well Services
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0377-0182 on 2026-04-23
**Report written:** 30 Apr 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0377-0182 showed the wellhead at 31.2 °C with the air at 26.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit.
The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

## Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

## Parts and cost

| Item | USD |
|---|---|
| Electric motor (exchange unit) | 3,971 |
| V-belts | 794 |
| Electrical connectors | 530 |
| Labour (company crew and contractor) | 4,364 |
| **Total** | **9,659** |

## Compliance check

| Protocol | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| WS-01 | Met | Meeting held and recorded |
| WS-02 | Met | Energy isolated and tagged |
| WS-03 | Met | Monitors bump-tested; highest 2 ppm |
| WS-07 | Met | Written 1 day after the work (limit 3 days) |

## Notes and recommendations

- Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
- Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0400-025

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0400-0181 on 2026-04-23

## What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0400-0181 showed the wellhead at 23.7 °C with the air at 21.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 7 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0409-027

**Asset:** WELL-0409 (NW-12 Well 409, T350, Northwest Block 12)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 02 May 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 13 May 2026 14:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 270 hours
**Crew lead:** Brian Coleman (U-304) · **Crew:** Daniel Foster · **Contractor:** Coyote Ridge Well Services
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0409-0181 on 2026-04-30
**Report written:** 13 May 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0409-0181 showed the wellhead at 30.6 °C with the air at 29.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

## Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

## Parts and cost

| Item | USD |
|---|---|
| Saddle bearing assembly | 962 |
| Bolts, shims and seals | 241 |
| Bearing grease and consumables | 401 |
| Labour (company crew and contractor) | 1,872 |
| **Total** | **3,476** |

## Compliance check

| Protocol | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| WS-01 | Met | Meeting held and recorded |
| WS-02 | Met | Energy isolated and tagged |
| WS-03 | Met | Monitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm |
| WS-07 | Met | Written the same day as the work (limit 3 days) |

## Notes and recommendations

- Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
- Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0404-030

**Asset:** WELL-0404 (NW-12 Well 404, T200, Northwest Block 12)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 07 Jun 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 23 Jun 2026 03:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 379 hours
**Crew lead:** Daniel Foster (U-302) · **Crew:** Kevin Price · **Contractor:** Coyote Ridge Well Services
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0404-0183 on 2026-06-04
**Report written:** 23 Jun 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0404-0183 showed the wellhead at 37.5 °C with the air at 34.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit.
The well stayed shut in for about 14 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

## Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0328-0194 on 2026-07-30
**Report written:** 25 Aug 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0328-0194 showed the wellhead at 38.9 °C with the air at 39.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

## Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.
This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 238 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 190 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0328-031 (WS-06).

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0374-027

**Asset:** WELL-0374 (NW-12 Well 374, T200, Northwest Block 12)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 04 Sep 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 15 Sep 2026 13:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 269 hours
**Crew lead:** Brian Coleman (U-304) · **Crew:** Daniel Foster, Kevin Price · **Contractor:** Coyote Ridge Well Services
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0374-0202 on 2026-09-03
**Report written:** 16 Sep 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0374-0202 showed the wellhead at 35.5 °C with the air at 33.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

## Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.
This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

- Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
- Start a root-cause analysis for this equipment before the next repair is closed (well-type manual, section 10).

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0321-0173 showed the wellhead at 10.2 °C with the air at 6.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0320-025

**Equipment:** pump jack

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0320-0169 on 2026-02-26
**Report written:** 03 Mar 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0320-0169 showed the wellhead at 15.6 °C with the air at 13.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

## Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

5. Greased all structural bearings.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

## What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0318-0202 showed the wellhead at 37.0 °C with the air at 31.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

## Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

## Safety and permits

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0326-0204 on 2026-09-17
**Report written:** 14 Oct 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0326-0204 showed the wellhead at 39.6 °C with the air at 29.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 24 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

## Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

## Work done

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0425-0210 showed the wellhead at 19.3 °C with the air at 13.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0205-028

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0205-0198 showed the wellhead at 24.9 °C with the air at 25.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.
This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: ESP drive stopped, drive disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 239 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 191 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0520-026

**Asset:** WELL-0520 (SE-32 Well 520, T500, Southeast Block 32)
**Equipment:** flowline

**Crew lead:** Megan Ward (U-305) · **Crew:** Brian Coleman
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0520-0163 on 2026-01-01

## What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0520-0163 showed the wellhead at 11.7 °C with the air at 5.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 36 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.
This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 279 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 223 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0472-0136 showed the wellhead at 16.8 °C with the air at 16.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

5. Greased all structural bearings.

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0499-025

**Asset:** WELL-0499 (SE-32 Well 499, T200, Southeast Block 32)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 13 Jun 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 23 Jun 2026 03:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 235 hours
**Crew lead:** Brian Coleman (U-304) · **Crew:** Daniel Foster, Kevin Price · **Contractor:** Coyote Ridge Well Services
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0499-0187 on 2026-06-11
**Report written:** 25 Jun 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0499-0187 showed the wellhead at 36.3 °C with the air at 30.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

## Parts and cost

|---|---|
| Saddle bearing assembly | 1,794 |
| Bolts, shims and seals | 448 |
| Bearing grease and consumables | 748 |
| Labour (company crew and contractor) | 2,920 |
| **Total** | **5,910** |

| Protocol | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| WS-01 | Met | Meeting held and recorded |
| WS-02 | Met | Energy isolated and tagged |
| WS-03 | Met | Monitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm |
| WS-07 | Met | Written 2 days after the work (limit 3 days) |

## Notes and recommendations

- Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
- Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

**Asset:** WELL-0531 (SE-32 Well 531, T500, Southeast Block 32)
**Equipment:** flowline
**Work started:** 04 Jul 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 29 Jul 2026 16:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 608 hours
**Crew lead:** Megan Ward (U-305) · **Crew:** Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0531-0192 on 2026-07-02
**Report written:** 30 Jul 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0531-0192 showed the wellhead at 52.5 °C with the air at 37.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: ESP drive stopped, drive disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 274 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 219 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0531-025 (WS-06).

## Parts and cost

|---|---|
| Line pipe section | 1,219 |
| Welding consumables and coating | 731 |
| Excavation services | 488 |
| Labour (company crew) | 1,201 |
| **Total** | **3,639** |

## Compliance check

| Protocol | Result | Detail |

| WS-01 | Met | Meeting held and recorded |
| WS-02 | Met | Energy isolated and tagged |
| WS-03 | Met | Monitors bump-tested; highest 2 ppm |
| WS-04 | Met | Permit issued; gas test 3% LEL |

## Notes and recommendations

- Check wall thickness along the rest of this flowline.
- Consider corrosion inhibitor injection.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0543-029

**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 31 Jul 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 04 Aug 2026 16:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 104 hours
**Crew lead:** Megan Ward (U-305) · **Crew:** Brian Coleman, Kevin Price
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0543-0194 on 2026-07-30
**Report written:** 06 Aug 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0543-0194 showed the wellhead at 38.0 °C with the air at 33.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.
The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0543-029 (WS-06).

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0504-026

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0484-033

**Asset:** WELL-0484 (SE-32 Well 484, T200, Southeast Block 32)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 27 Dec 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 12 Jan 2027 23:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 399 hours
**Crew lead:** Brian Coleman (U-304) · **Crew:** Daniel Foster
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0484-0215 on 2026-12-24
**Report written:** 13 Jan 2027

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0484-0215 showed the wellhead at 16.7 °C with the air at 11.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.
This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

## What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0515-0173 showed the wellhead at 5.8 °C with the air at 6.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0579-0212 showed the wellhead at 8.7 °C with the air at 8.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

5. Greased all structural bearings.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0588-025

**Equipment:** flowline

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0588-0195 on 2026-07-16
**Report written:** 23 Jul 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0588-0195 showed the wellhead at 43.1 °C with the air at 33.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

## Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: ESP drive stopped, drive disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 246 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 197 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0588-025 (WS-06).

- Check wall thickness along the rest of this flowline.
- Consider corrosion inhibitor injection.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0459-025

**Asset:** WELL-0459 (SE-32 Well 459, T350, Southeast Block 32)
**Equipment:** pump jack

**Crew lead:** Daniel Foster (U-302) · **Crew:** Megan Ward, Brian Coleman
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0459-0200 on 2026-09-03
**Report written:** 17 Sep 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0459-0200 showed the wellhead at 31.9 °C with the air at 28.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

## Safety and permits

5. Greased all structural bearings.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0025-035

**Asset:** WELL-0025 (SW-23 Well 025, T350, Southwest Block 23)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 28 Nov 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 09 Dec 2026 14:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 270 hours
**Crew lead:** Kevin Price (U-303) · **Crew:** Megan Ward · **Contractor:** Coyote Ridge Well Services
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0025-0209 on 2026-11-26
**Report written:** 10 Dec 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0025-0209 showed the wellhead at 13.5 °C with the air at 9.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

**Asset:** WELL-0004 (SW-23 Well 004, T350, Southwest Block 23)
**Equipment:** pump jack
**Work started:** 21 Feb 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 17 Mar 2026 02:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 570 hours
**Crew lead:** Kevin Price (U-303) · **Crew:** Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0004-0172 on 2026-02-19
**Report written:** 18 Mar 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0004-0172 showed the wellhead at 18.7 °C with the air at 8.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.
The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

## Parts and cost

| Item | USD |
|---|---|
| Saddle bearing assembly | 1,534 |
| Bolts, shims and seals | 384 |
| Bearing grease and consumables | 639 |
| Labour (company crew) | 2,629 |
| **Total** | **5,186** |

## Compliance check

| Protocol | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| WS-01 | Met | Meeting held and recorded |
| WS-02 | Met | Energy isolated and tagged |
| WS-03 | Met | Monitors bump-tested; highest 2 ppm |
| WS-07 | Met | Written 1 day after the work (limit 3 days) |

## Notes and recommendations

- Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
- Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0020-030

## What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0020-0175 showed the wellhead at 8.5 °C with the air at 9.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.
The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

## Safety and permits

## Work done

1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

## Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0043-029

**Equipment:** flowline
**Work started:** 01 May 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 04 May 2026 21:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 85 hours
**Crew lead:** Kevin Price (U-303) · **Crew:** Megan Ward
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0043-0179 on 2026-04-30
**Report written:** 05 May 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0043-0179 showed the wellhead at 30.6 °C with the air at 27.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 261 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 209 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

- Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0043-029 (WS-06).

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0041-0195 on 2026-07-30
**Report written:** 20 Aug 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0041-0195 showed the wellhead at 43.5 °C with the air at 38.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 17 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

## Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.
This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0088-031

**Asset:** WELL-0088 (SW-24 Well 088, T350, Southwest Block 24)
**Equipment:** flowline
**Work started:** 05 Jul 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 14 Jul 2026 09:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 217 hours
**Crew lead:** Brian Coleman (U-304) · **Crew:** Kevin Price · **Contractor:** Tumbleweed Flowline Co.
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0088-0193 on 2026-07-02
**Report written:** 15 Jul 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0088-0193 showed the wellhead at 46.6 °C with the air at 37.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 7 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

## Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.
This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 284 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 227 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

## Waste

- Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0088-031 (WS-06).

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0268-0191 showed the wellhead at 38.3 °C with the air at 34.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. ## Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

## Safety and permits

## Work done

1. Disconnected and removed the motor.

**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0085-0197 on 2026-09-03

## What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0085-0197 showed the wellhead at 33.8 °C with the air at 34.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.
The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

## Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.
This is corrective repair number 7 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

- Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

## Work done

1. Excavated around the leak.
2. Cut out the corroded section.
3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
4. Coated the new joint.
5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

## Testing and return to service

Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0300-033

**Asset:** WELL-0300 (SW-24 Well 300, T350, Southwest Block 24)
**Equipment:** wellhead
**Work started:** 29 Nov 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 08 Dec 2026 12:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 220 hours
**Crew lead:** Daniel Foster (U-302) · **Crew:** Kevin Price, Brian Coleman · **Contractor:** Coyote Ridge Well Services
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0300-0209 on 2026-11-26
**Report written:** 09 Dec 2026

## What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0300-0209 showed the wellhead at 15.2 °C with the air at 11.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored.
The well stayed shut in for about 7 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

## Root cause

Normal packing wear.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
2. Removed the old packing.
3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

## Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

| Absorbent pads | 152 |

| **Total** | **937** |

## Notes and recommendations

# Maintenance Report — MNT-0056-032

**Asset:** WELL-0056 (SW-24 Well 056, T350, Southwest Block 24)
**Equipment:** separator
**Work started:** 26 Dec 2026 08:00 · **Finished:** 13 Jan 2027 16:00 · **Well stopped for this job:** 440 hours
**Crew lead:** Daniel Foster (U-302) · **Crew:** Brian Coleman
**Triggered by:** inspection INS-0056-0216 on 2026-12-24
**Report written:** 13 Jan 2027

## What happened

Field staff reported that the separator was overfilling and the dump valve was not opening. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0056-0216 showed the wellhead at 20.8 °C with the air at 12.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The level controller had failed.
The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

## Root cause

Paraffin build-up stopped the float from moving.

## Safety and permits

- Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
- Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
- Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

## Work done

1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
2. Replaced the level controller.
3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

## Testing and return to service

Cycled the separator three times; level control worked correctly. The well was returned to production.

## Parts and cost

| Gaskets and fittings | 653 |
| Labour (company crew) | 1,692 |
| **Total** | **4,957** |

| WS-02 | Met | Energy isolated and tagged |
| WS-03 | Met | Monitors bump-tested; highest 2 ppm |
| WS-07 | Met | Written the same day as the work (limit 3 days) |

## Notes and recommendations

- Add the separator controller to the quarterly checklist.
